Dev, Mateo — can you both attend? Mateo I expect you'll take system/runtime design and Dev you'll take perf/ops and quantization tradeoffs. Priyom, I'm looping you in as bar-raiser; would appreciate a short alignment call to calibrate on leveling and the key failure modes we should look for.

Proposal for a 25-minute prep call: Fri 8/13 12:45–1:10pm PT (right before the loop). If that works, I'll send the Zoom link and the scorecard template.

Quick notes on role scope (high level):
- Ownership: production inference runtime (low-latency, multi-tenant serving)
- Impact: reduce per-token cost via batching/kv cache improvements, kernel selection heuristics
- Leadership: technical mentorship and runbook ownership; not a people-manager role initially

Key leveling signals to discuss: breadth vs. depth in runtime internals, demonstrated tradeoffs across cost/latency/reliability, prior mentorship & cross-team influence.

I attached the current job brief (staff_serving_job_brief_v2.pdf) and the scorecard I typically use (interview_scorecard_staff_serving.docx). Please review prior to the prep call and flag any must-ask questions.

Subject: Re: Candidate intro + scheduling: Jordan Liu (Staff Serving Engineer)

Evelyn — confirmed for Fri 1:30–2:45pm PT. I'll take the system design + runtime internals portion.

Preliminary focus areas / sample prompts I'm planning to use:
- System design: design a multi-tenant inference service that supports dynamic batching and prefixed caching. Ask for design decisions and failure modes under heavy tail latency.
- Runtime internals: deep dive into attention cache structure, kv cache invalidation across model versions, and GPU memory management for mixed-precision quantized models.
- Performance tradeoffs: how they'd tune kernel selection given a mix of short chat-like requests and longer batch jobs.

Leveling notes: for Staff we should expect concrete prior ownership (e.g., shipped a runtime feature that materially reduced p95 latency or cost) and evidence of driving cross-team standards. If the answers are purely academic without measurable impact, that's a red flag.

I'll add two specific test prompts to the doc: one around cold-start batching and one around cache invalidation across model rollouts.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez

Thanks for looping me in, Evelyn. I can do the bar-raiser slot on the loop. Two quick asks before the prep call: 

1) Please confirm the rubric thresholds for Staff vs Senior (i.e., what are must-have vs nice-to-have). My baseline:
   - Must-have: ownership of a production runtime feature, evidence of tradeoffs with metrics, cross-team influence
   - Nice-to-have: published benchmarks or OSS contributions, experience with custom kernel work
2) Can we standardize the specific scoring buckets we'll use during the loop? I prefer the 1–4 scale in the attached scorecard, with explicit notes for what 1 vs 4 means per dimension.

I'll review Jordan's resume now; if anything jumps out I'll ping offline.

Also: happy to run a 20–25 minute prep sync at 12:45 PT — that timing works for me.

—Priyom

- Runtime/perf (Dev): 20–25 min; prioritize concrete optimizations and metrics (p50/p95 improvements).
- Leadership/decision-making (Priyom): 15–20 min; probe how decisions were made, tradeoffs communicated, and technical influence enacted.

Candidate: Jordan, we look forward to meeting you — you'll receive a separate calendar invite from HiringOps with the loop details. Please join the prep call at 12:45 PT if you're available; otherwise we'll see you at 1:30 PT for the loop.
